name.description: Name for a source-supported connection lifecycle. A connection-oriented channel represents one connection lifecycle, beginning with a source-supported connect or listen step and ending with transport close. A reconnect or session-resumption connection uses a different channel even when the parties, addresses, ports, or logical session are unchanged. Distinguish initial and resumed connections. Reuse message definitions, but create channel-specific steps for their exchanges. Preserve cross-channel prerequisites, state, and field relations supported by the source. Describe how earlier exchanges supply or derive values used on a later channel; distinguish direct reuse from derivation without assuming equality. Do not require the initial connection to close before resumption unless the source requires that order. A persistent listener need not listen again for every connection; listening readiness is distinct from an accepted connection. Do not invent missing network operations or expand arbitrary repetitions into infinitely many channels: model the distinct source-supported lifecycle roles and record any unspecified boundaries as unresolved. For connectionless channels, follow source-defined exchange boundaries without inventing connect or close. Reviewer: check lifecycle boundaries, separate resumption channels, and the cross-channel state needed to perform them.

action.description: A step action is send, listen, connect, or close. send is one protocol message between a sender and a receiver. listen means that party starts listening and can accept connections. connect means that party opens the connection. close means that party closes the transport connection. Protocol termination messages stay send; add a separate close step only when the source describes the later transport close. Do not invent a message, sender, or receiver for a network action. Keep one network-action node per party, channel, and action. The same node may occur more than once in an ordered trace. Put occurrence-specific conditions on dependency edges or proposal constraints, not by copying the node. Do not add listen, connect, or close steps when the source does not describe them.

name.description: Short protocol term. Reuse the same message's name. A message is an actual protocol message or RFC-defined independently exchanged transfer unit. Grammar productions and table classification labels do not automatically constitute messages. Abstract categories, command groups, fields and syntax components are not independent message types. Ordinary message types need not carry associated fields. A concrete response code defines a separate message type only when its response carries associated fields needed in later interactions for correlation, connection setup, branching or interaction state. The response code itself or free-form reply wording alone does not justify a separate type; otherwise reuse an actually exchanged, source-supported shared response form, not a response-code family or classification label.

associated_fields.description: Attach a field only to the message that actually transmits it. Retain only fields needed for cross-message correlation, connection setup, interaction branching or interaction state. A message that triggers another message does not inherit that message's fields. Do not extract complete wire layouts or ordinary payload details.
